standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies Der_k(O_X, O_X) with Hom(omega_X, O_X) via D = theta composed with d, and makes dz a basis of Omega at a closed point for a uniformizer z.

standard_prerequisites.name: Global sections of invertible sheaves on curves

core_obligations: Identification (proof lines 6891-6897): D = theta composed with d with theta in Hom(Omega_{X/k}, O_X) = Hom(omega_X, O_X), and deg(omega_X) = 2g - 2.
Genus at least 2 (proof lines 6897-6901): the sheaf omega_X^tensor -1 has negative degree, so theta = 0 and Der = 0.

Genus 1 and 0 (proof lines 6902-6912): in genus 1 a nonzero theta is nowhere vanishing; in genus 0 it vanishes on a divisor of degree 2; vanishing of theta at a closed point x is equivalent to D fixing x because for a uniformizer z the differential dz is a basis of Omega_{X,x} and D(z) = theta(dz).
proof_roadmap: Move derivations to Hom(omega_X, O_X) through the universal derivation.
Kill the sheaf Hom by negative degree in genus at least 2.
Control the zero divisor of theta in genus 1 and genus 0.
Translate vanishing of theta into the fixed-point condition via a uniformizer.
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the tangent space of a smooth proper curve in each genus (statement lines 6878-6889). The proof (lines 6891-6912) is complete: the derivation-identification, the degree computation killing Hom(omega, O) for g >= 2, the nowhere-vanishing versus degree-two-divisor behaviour in genus 1 and 0, and the uniformizer translation of the fixed-point condition. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: degree bookkeeping on invertible sheaves with a clean local translation at the end.
